ghi_chu.mo_ta: The man at the far left wears a black hat with a wide brim that looks turned up, close to a tricorn.
ghi_chu.ly_do: The tricorn became fashionable in the 1690s and later. In 1666 men wore broad-brimmed, high-crowned hats that were not cocked into three corners.

ghi_chu.mo_ta: The skyline on the right has tall, flat-topped, boxy tower blocks with a square tower and a thin spire. They look like Victorian or modern rectangular buildings.
ghi_chu.ly_do: The skyline of London in 1666 was medieval and Tudor, made up of timber-framed houses and church steeples. It had no tall, uniform, multi-storey block towers.

ghi_chu.mo_ta: The central skyline has slender Gothic needle spires, one of them a very tall pointed spire at about x=0.45.
ghi_chu.ly_do: Old St Paul's had lost its spire in 1561. A tall, thin Gothic spire of this kind does not match the 1666 skyline, and the look is more Victorian Gothic Revival.
